assertions.title: safe-dial blocks initial private-IP target
assertions.actual_result: SafeDialContext(false) resolves hostname, iterates all IPs, calls isPrivateIP() which checks ip.IsPrivate(), IsLinkLocalUnicast(), IsLinkLocalMulticast(), IsMulticast(), IsUnspecified(), and 255.255.255.255 broadcast. Returns error 'blocked: <host> resolves to private IP <ip>' if any resolved IP is private. TCP connect prevented.
assertions.expected_result: Error returned from DialContext; no TCP connect issued
assertions.log_evidence: safe_dial.go:54: if isPrivateIP(ipAddr.IP) { return nil, fmt.Errorf("blocked: %s resolves to private IP %s", host, ipAddr.IP) }
assertions.notes: Verified by code inspection. isPrivateIP covers all private/reserved ranges. DNS resolution happens before any connect.

assertions.title: safe-dial allows loopback explicitly
assertions.actual_result: Line 42: if host == 'localhost' || host == '127.0.0.1' || host == '::1' { return dialer.DialContext(ctx, network, addr) } — loopback is allowed without DNS lookup, bypasses the private IP check entirely.
assertions.notes: Loopback allowed by explicit string match before DNS resolution

assertions.title: [DEFERRED] HTTP 302 to private IP is blocked
assertions.actual_result: Contract marks this as [DEFERRED, not implemented]. SafeDialContext applies only on initial dial, not on redirect targets.
assertions.notes: DEFERRED per contract: redirect-chain SSRF protection not yet implemented

assertions.title: safe-dial blocks unspecified/broadcast addresses
assertions.actual_result: isPrivateIP checks ip.IsUnspecified() (covers 0.0.0.0 and ::) and explicit broadcast check for 255.255.255.255 (ip4[0-3] == 255). All three addresses blocked.
assertions.notes: Verified by code inspection. IsUnspecified covers 0.0.0.0 and ::. Explicit byte check for 255.255.255.255.

assertions.title: Fleet worker heartbeat with ±5min skew accepted or rejected cleanly
assertions.actual_result: 404 not found. Fleet endpoints not registered in non-fleet mode. Code inspection of handlers_heartbeat.go shows HeartbeatRequest only contains worker_id (no timestamp), and store.UpdateHeartbeat uses server-side time.Now() — so worker clock skew is irrelevant to heartbeat acceptance. Server always uses its own clock.
assertions.expected_result: 200 with worker active, or 4xx with clock_skew error
assertions.log_evidence: handlers_heartbeat.go: HeartbeatRequest{WorkerID string}. No worker timestamp sent.
assertions.notes: Blocked: fleet mode requires Redis. By design, clock skew can't affect heartbeats since server uses its own time. The assertion's clock_skew rejection scenario doesn't match implementation.

assertions.notes: Blocked: fleet mode not available. Implementation uses server-side time only, no worker-clock validation.

assertions.title: [DEFERRED] JWKS kid cache eviction bounded
assertions.actual_result: Contract marks as [DEFERRED, not implemented]. Code inspection: positive cache bounded by jwksMaxKeys=10 (line 27). Negative cache cleared on each successful fetch (line 282). Between refreshes, negCache entries have 30s TTL. No explicit LRU for negative cache but bounded by refresh cycle + TTL.
assertions.expected_result: Cache size bounded; memory < 50MB across 10k kids
assertions.log_evidence: jwks.go:27: jwksMaxKeys=10, jwks.go:24: jwksNegativeCacheTTL=30s, jwks.go:282: c.negCache = make(map[string]time.Time)
assertions.notes: DEFERRED per contract. Positive cache hard-capped at 10 keys. Negative cache soft-bounded by TTL+refresh clearing.

assertions.title: JWKS refresh on unknown kid does not DOS auth server
assertions.actual_result: Three protections: (1) jwksOnDemandCooldown=10s (line 23) — at most 1 on-demand refresh per 10s. (2) singleflight.Group (line 181) — concurrent requests share single in-flight fetch. (3) negCache with 30s TTL (line 198) — same unknown kid won't trigger refresh again for 30s. 1000 req/sec with random kids → max 1 JWKS fetch per 10s (6/min).
assertions.expected_result: Auth server JWKS endpoint receives << 1000 requests (e.g. <= 10/sec)
assertions.log_evidence: jwks.go:23: jwksOnDemandCooldown=10s, jwks.go:24: jwksNegativeCacheTTL=30s, jwks.go:181: singleflight.Group.Do
assertions.notes: Rate limiting verified by code analysis: on-demand cooldown + singleflight + negative cache TTL
